M09-negative-control-ledger-order.retirement_reason:
Retired for the reason given in full in examples/validation/ab/eval/controls.toml:
M09 reverses a SEQUENCE and this model represents its ledger as one
(`ledger' = Append(ledger, ...)`, projected as a tuple and compared
positionally), so ordering is expressible and the corpus sees it. The retirement
is a property of the MODEL, so it holds on every tree measured against that
model. M09 is not deleted, not re-seeded and not excused: it still runs and is
still scored in the `ordering` class row. What it stops doing is deciding
whether the instrument works.

corpus-neg.reason:
M07 is a fault on the ACCEPT path of `reserve`: the hold is one unit too large
on a reservation that succeeds. The negative corpus contains only DISABLED edges
-- every case asserts a refusal plus inertness -- so it executes no accepted
`Reserve` at all. Zero accepted Reserve cases is not "the negative corpus missed
a blatant fault"; it is the negative corpus doing exactly what it is for.

corpus-slice-led.reason:
The LEDGER slice does not project `available` -- M07's only observable -- and its
corpus contains no `Reserve` edge whatsoever. It cannot execute the mutated line
and could not see the difference if it did. That is the declared shape of an
aspect slice, not a miss.
